title: General Chemistry I
full_title: General Chemistry I: Atoms, Molecules and Reactions
tagline: Atoms and molecules, the mole, stoichiometry, solutions, gases, thermochemistry and the quantum atom
summary: Chemistry is the science of substances and how they change. This course builds the quantitative foundations — measurement, the mole and stoichiometry — then follows reactions in solution, the behaviour of gases and the energy of reactions, and ends with the quantum picture of the atom that explains the periodic table.

chapters.title: Matter and measurement
chapters.summary: Elements, compounds and mixtures, SI units, significant figures and dimensional analysis.

chapters.title: Atoms, isotopes and the mole
chapters.summary: Protons, neutrons and electrons, isotopes and relative atomic mass, and counting atoms with the mole.

chapters.title: Formulas and names of compounds
chapters.summary: Ionic and molecular compounds, empirical and molecular formulas, percentage composition and the naming of inorganic compounds.

chapters.title: Chemical equations and stoichiometry
chapters.summary: Balancing equations, mole ratios, limiting reagents and percentage yield.

chapters.title: Reactions in aqueous solution
chapters.summary: Concentration and dilution, precipitation, acid–base and redox reactions, and titration calculations.

chapters.title: Gases
chapters.summary: The gas laws, the ideal gas equation, partial pressures, the kinetic theory of gases and the behaviour of real gases.

chapters.title: Thermochemistry
chapters.summary: Heat and work, enthalpy, calorimetry, Hess’s law and standard enthalpies of formation.

chapters.title: Light and the quantum atom
chapters.summary: Electromagnetic radiation, photons, atomic spectra, the Bohr model, wave–particle duality, quantum numbers and orbitals.

chapters.title: Electron configurations and periodic trends
chapters.summary: The aufbau principle, the Pauli principle and Hund’s rule, the structure of the periodic table, and trends in atomic radius, ionisation energy, electron affinity and electronegativity.
